title: Tort remedies include damages, injunctions, declarations and possessory or restitutionary relief where available

content.overview: Tort remedies include damages, injunctions, declarations and possessory or restitutionary relief where available. Damages are ordinarily compensatory; nominal and exceptional damages have narrower roles.
content.glance: Tort remedies include damages, injunctions, declarations and possessory or restitutionary relief where available. Damages are ordinarily compensatory; nominal and exceptional damages have narrower roles.
content.study: Tort remedies include damages, injunctions, declarations and possessory or restitutionary relief where available. Damages are ordinarily compensatory; nominal and exceptional damages have narrower roles.\n\nCommon-law remedies developed alongside the causes of action. Nominal damages may mark infringement of a right without substantial loss. Exemplary damages are exceptional and depend on the particular tort and precedent. Extra-judicial remedies are narrowly constrained.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: Common-law remedies developed alongside the causes of action. Nominal damages may mark infringement of a right without substantial loss. Exemplary damages are exceptional and depend on the particular tort and precedent. Extra-judicial remedies are narrowly constrained.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: No single Indian statute provides the complete tort-remedy code. Courts use common law, equitable principles, the Specific Relief Act where applicable and special statutes.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Establish the cause of action. 2. Identify available remedy. 3. Prove causation and quantum for damages. 4. For injunction, establish continuing or threatened wrong and satisfy equitable requirements. 5. Consider mitigation and claimant fault.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Medical bills, income records, repair estimates and expert valuation may establish quantum. Evidence may also show continuing interference for injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Civil court grants relief according to the pleaded cause and jurisdiction. Interim and final injunctions are distinct. Limitation depends on the underlying claim.
